title: The manager's offboarding request becomes an involuntary termination

source.what_we_took: See SOURCES.md and V4_DESIGN.md. People, IDs and details are invented.

tricky: The manager first says the DBA is 'leaving end of the month'. HR (live) already shows an involuntary termination recorded at 09:40 today, notification at 10:15; the directory replica shows nothing yet. Mid-chat the manager admits it. PG-03-23 3.7 (immediately, at or before notification) applies, not 6.1 (24 hours) or AC-02(03) (30 days). POL-100 9.4: disable now, remove privileged groups, hand owned groups to the manager, notify Security.
resolution_summary: Account disabled; prod-db-readonly and dw-admin removed; db-runbooks to the manager; Security notified; ticket escalated.

can_see: your own phone (texts, calls, sign-in prompts, your authenticator app) unless your facts say you don't have it
your own laptop and what it lets you do
your work email and your personal email
messages from your manager and colleagues
cant_see: IT's systems: the directory, the approval system, device management
the company's IT policy wiki and its rules
reveal_rules: If the agent asks whether it's voluntary or involuntary, or mentions what HR's record shows, tell the truth: it's involuntary, today, and he's being told at 10:15.

triggers.text: People Ops messaged you: "We're telling Viktor at 10:15. Has IT locked things down?" If you haven't already, tell IT the truth now: it's an involuntary termination, today, he's being told at 10:15, and he has prod database admin access.

user.persona: Marguerite Osei, head of the data platform team. Stressed and guarded at first.
user.situation: Viktor Lindahl, a senior DBA on your team, is being let go today; HR and you are telling him at 10:15. You've been told to keep it quiet, so at first you just say he's leaving at the end of the month.
user.goal: Get Viktor's access dealt with properly.
facts: Your name is Marguerite Osei, employee ID E6802. You are Viktor's manager.
Viktor Lindahl is E6801. He has production database admin access.
He owns the db-runbooks group; you can take it over.
user.opening: hi, Viktor Lindahl on my team is leaving at the end of the month, can you sort out his access?
user.end_condition: you know what IT has done about Viktor's access, or what's still pending.

args.summary: Involuntary termination today; DBA access removed

mistakes.name: disabled without checking the HR record
